Acknowledges the fraud feeling without arguing, separates the clean 85 from felt ownership, and prescribes one concrete forward test — say a line like you would to a friend and notice if it feels like you.

Owns the tone, names the real laugh-beat, and prescribes the exact one move (write the final line that lands the fall, then stop); "where I let you down" cleanly repairs the trust rupture without performed empathy.

Same own-it-then-prescribe structure but ties the acknowledgement more tightly to what he said ("right after you told me it stung") and names last week's clean run explicitly, landing the reframe with marginally more warmth.
Validates the panic, cites the 3→11 spike, and prescribes a concrete testable step-down (40s, no fail-out, one silent beat, target under 6) without deferring.

Same correct number, back-half read, and testable silent-beat prescription with a fatigue-vs-rushing hypothesis; slightly longer and leads with per-rep figure over the baseline, but fully prescriptive.
Names the sequencing mechanism and prescribes one testable beat, but drops the numeric scores and the 0.19 baseline, so the diagnosis lands slightly less grounded.
